sentences.text: The offences alleged against him are under Sections 376(2)(n), 323 and 342 IPC.
2. The prosecution case is that the petitioner committed rape upon his step daughter on various occasions at the residence, where both of them have been living.
It is also alleged that on 07.03.2023, the petitioner inflicted voluntary hurt upon the de facto complainant, by hitting upon her face and kicking upon her chest and abdomen.
3. The case has been registered by the Kadavanthra Police on 09.04.2023 on the basis of the First Information Statement given by the de facto complainant.
After the completion of investigation, the Final Report in this case has been filed by the Inspector of Police, Kadavanthra Police Station.
4. In the present petition, the petitioner would contend that he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is stated that the petitioner strongly opposed an affair which the de facto complainant maintained 2025:KER:58972 with a person, who was having connections with a banned outfit, and that he strongly deprecated the above conduct of the de facto complainant.
According to the petitioner, the de facto complainant was compelled to prefer a false complaint against him under the instigation of the above person, with whom she was in love.

Later on, the de facto complainant is said to have realised the gross mistake which she committed, and sent repeated letters to the Commissioner of Police, Asst. Commissioner of Police as well as the SHO of Police, urging them to withdraw from the proceedings being initiated against the petitioner.

When the petitioner filed an Anticipatory Bail Application, the de facto complainant filed an affidavit stating that he has been falsely implicated in this case, and hence the above Bail Application has to be decided in his favour.

For the verification of the correctness of the above affidavit, which the de facto complainant had filed, the learned Single Judge of this Court, who has been dealing with the Anticipatory Bail Application, is seen to have heard the de facto complainant in person, and ascertained the correctness of her contentions in the affidavit that she happened to prefer a false complaint against the petitioner.
Thus, it is stated that it is highly necessary that the proceedings against the petitioner have to be quashed, to meet the ends of justice.
2025:KER:58972  5. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor representing the State of Kerala.  6.

It is seen from the records that the de facto complainant has filed three affidavits exculpating the petitioner from the allegations which happened to be raised against him, leading to the registration of this crime.

In addition to that,
Annexures A2 to A5 would reveal that she had sent letters to the police officers, from the Commissioner of Police to the SI of Police, urging the above officers to drop the proceedings being initiated against the petitioner, since she happened to prefer a false complaint against him.

Annexure A9 affidavit, which the de facto complainant had sworn on 20.12.2023, contain statement to the effect that the petitioner has not committed any of the offences as alleged in this case, and that the registration of this Crime was actually the outcome of the mistake which she committed Biju vs State Of Kerala on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138061262/
2 under the compulsion of her lover and the persons behind him.

7. A reading of Annexure 10 order passed by this Court on 22.01.2024 in BA No.10359/2023 would reveal that the learned Judge had occasion to interact with the de facto complainant in person and to ascertain from her that she has no complaints against the petitioner, and that she happened to prefer a false complaint in view of her affair with 2025:KER:58972 the lover.
It is by taking note of the above aspects that Anticipatory Bail was granted to the petitioner.
8. Having regard to the above facts and circumstances of the case, the contention of the petitioner that a false case happened to be foisted against him, cannot be ignored.

There is absolutely no reason to discard the three affidavits, which the de facto complainant has filed on three different occasions, exculpating the petitioner from the insinuations alleged in this crime.
So also, the fact that a learned Single Judge of this Court dealing with Bail Application had the occasion to interact with the victim and to ascertain the actual truth from her, cannot be ignored.
In that view of the matter, the prayer of the petitioner, to quash the proceedings against him, requires a favourable consideration.
In the result, the petition stands allowed.

The proceedings against the petitioner/accused in CP No.49/2024 on the files of Judicial First Class Magistrate Court VIII, Ernakulam, which arose out of Crime No.364/2023 of Kadavanthra Police Station, Ernakulam, are hereby quashed.
